item.title: The Israeli military wants several more weeks to fight Iran war, officials say
item.summary: The Israeli military estimates it would need several more weeks of fighting to complete its war goals in Iran, at a time when President Trump says the U.S. is negotiating an end to the war.

item.title: Pakistan is poised to host the U.S. and Iran for talks to end the war
item.summary: The Pakistani prime minister said his country stands ready to host negotiations toward a settlement as the war with Iran nears the one-month mark.

item.title: Airstrikes may have destroyed Iran's last F-14s, ending a long, strange saga
item.summary: The F-14 was made famous in Top Gun. The U.S. sold the planes to Iran in the 1970s, only for the two countries to become enemies. Iran kept its F-14s flying for decades in the face of U.S. sanctions.

item.title: Kim vows to 'irreversibly' cement North Korea's nuclear status
item.summary: In his speech, Kim expressed pride in the country's rapid expansion of nuclear weapons and missiles in recent years, calling it the "right" choice.

item.title: Senate confirms Trump's pick for new role of fraud enforcement at Justice Department
item.summary: The confirmation comes just days after the White House announced details of its own task force to pursue fraud in government programs.

item.title: Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon
item.summary: Pulido has been a mainstay of Tejano music —a genre blending traditional regional Mexican elements with country, pop and conjunto influences — for more than three decades.

item.title: Trump takes aim at windmills despite increasing energy costs
item.summary: President Trump's mission to fight renewable wind energy comes at a time of rising energy costs.

item.title: Congress loses a flying perk as DHS shutdown continues
item.summary: Delta Airlines is temporarily suspending specialty services to member of Congress due to resource constraints from the ongoing shutdown of DHS.

item.title: Her mother murdered her father in an infamous case. Now, she's telling her own story
item.summary: Lucille Miller was convicted of killing her husband in 1965. Now her daughter Debra reflects on her own traumatic childhood and its lingering effects in The Most Wonderful Terrible Person.

item.title: A professional cornhole player and quadruple amputee is arrested for murder
item.summary: Dayton Webber, 27, is accused of shooting a man in his car during an argument. He has shared his story of becoming a pro athlete after losing his arms and legs to a childhood bacterial infection.
